newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent higher on fresh heating oil spurt.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent higher on fresh heating oil spurt.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures hit new highs for the day as NYMEX contracts opened strongly led yet again by heating oil.
Nov Brent hit a high of $24.25 in the first hour of NYMEX trading and at 1445 GMT was up 36 cents at $24.21.
"It's just more of the same," said an IPE broker. "People buying heating oil."
NYMEX crude got a psychologial boost breaking above $25 a barrel.

The first chill of winter weather over the weekend in the U.S. northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, exacerbated worries about inventories of heating oil which are already running about one third down on last year.

Meteorologist Weather Services Corp said temperatures in the U.S. northeast were as much as seven degrees Celsius (14 Fahrenheit) below normal at the weekend but were expected to return to normal during the week.
Oct gas oil rose $2.50 a tonne to $248 but lost ground versus November as dealers rolled forward long positions ahead of the October contract expiry on Thursday.
The Oct/Nov gas oil spread narrowed $3.50 to $6.50 as Nov gas oil went up $6 to $241.50 a tonne.
Gas oil's spread over crude for November extended five-year record highs to $8.20 a barrel.
